items.title: In the random subgraph of a high-dimensional product graph there is typically no component whose order lies in the interval from two to d to the twentieth
items.author: Sahar Diskin, Anna Geisler
items.work: \vspace{-1.5cm}Perfect Matching in Product Graphs\\ and in their Random Subgraphs
items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the gap lemma for component orders (author lemma at source lines 514-516, label lem:component-gap): with high probability the random subgraph has no component whose order lies between 2 and d^20. The proof (source lines 518-532) is a first-moment computation whose content is the combination of two estimates: the expansion bound e_G(K,K^c) >= 0.9kd for sets of that size, coming from the author's displayed expansion estimate, and the rooted-tree bound that turns the event of K being a component into the product n(ed)^{k-1}(1-p)^{0.9kd}, after which the author substitutes 2 <= k <= d^20, n(1-p)^d <= d^{1/50} and d = Theta_M(log n) to reach n^{1-0.8k} and concludes with a union bound over k (proof lines 525-532). The estimates are quantitative and are the substance of the argument. H2.
